methodology.boundary: client-observed complete local HTTP request duration via loopback; server duration_ms recorded nowhere as a benchmark number and never called inference latency
methodology.percentile_method: NumPy linear percentile, one consistent method for every operation
methodology.warmup_policy: per-operation warm-ups excluded from statistics (cheap 5, MC-1k 2, MC-10k 1, strategy 1, frontend 5)
methodology.outlier_policy: no samples discarded; failures recorded separately (zero failures in all operations)
methodology.rerun_note: container run executed twice: first attempt completed all 11 backend operations green but the script crashed before persisting when JSON-parsing frontend HTML; after adding a raw-HTML timing path the entire container operation was rerun; no cherry-picking between runs
methodology.determinism_note: artifact schema and methodology are deterministic; timing values are measured empirical evidence and are not byte-reproducible across runs
methodology.p99_note: operations with fewer than 100 samples report an empirical percentile over a limited sample, not a production SLO; no throughput derived from latency

limitations: all numbers are LOCAL loopback evidence, never cloud or network latency
no browser engine: frontend numbers are LOCAL FRONTEND SERVER RESPONSE TIME only, never page load, render, hydration, or Core Web Vitals
server duration_ms is endpoint duration, never model inference latency
readiness may use its internal readiness cache
p99 over fewer than 100 samples is empirical, not an SLO
no throughput, requests-per-second, or load-test claims
container timings include Docker Desktop virtualization overhead on macOS
benchmark machine only (Apple M4, 10 CPUs); other hardware differs
